# About this proof {kicker="Template proof"}

This booklet is a proof of the manual's PDF template, not the manual. Each component appears at least once with
real data: a faction opener, unit cards with their stat panels, a narrator's essay with a drop cap and a pull quote,
a unit tree, a tech tree, a tip and a field note. Values were copied by hand from the generated tables for this
proof; the chapters will take them from the generator's data file, so no chapter types a number.

The bars in a card's stat panel measure a unit against the strongest of its own faction: a full health bar is the
faction's toughest unit, not the toughest in the game.

::: {.tip title="reading the booklet"}
On screen, view two pages side by side with the cover alone: the spreads are laid out as pairs. To print, run
`impose.sh` on the PDF and print the result double-sided, flipped on the short edge, then fold and staple.
:::

::: {.fieldnote title="the edge tabs"}
Each corporation's chapters carry a coloured tab on the fore-edge at a height of their own. With the booklet
closed, the tabs show where each faction's pages begin.
:::

# Synthexis {.opener faction="synthexis" kicker="The corporations"}

> Engineered to adapt.

Synthexis is a bioengineering company. It does not mine or build factories. It takes over a field of biter
spawners, feeds it on your pollution and breeds biters of its own, tinted green and yellow. Its waves are planned:
they pick a way in, go for what keeps your turrets firing, and change after every attack that fails.

## What it breeds

::: {.unit unit="lp-bred-big-biter"}
Most of any grown wave. A bred big biter costs the culture a little biomass and nothing else, so the culture
spends them freely.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-bred-cinder"}
Bred for walls that have held. It walks up to the wall at a run and bursts there, and a well-aimed group takes the
corner turrets with it.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-bred-spore"}
The one breed that looks up. It travels with waves sent against a base that defends itself with drones and
robots.
:::

::: {.tip}
Kill the biochamber beside an incubator and the incubator stops breeding. A biochamber under attack does not call
the wave home, so it is the quiet target while a wave is out.
:::

::: {.lore kicker="From the archive" title="The culture" draft="Draft" faction="synthexis"}
Synthexis came to the planet with no drills and no furnaces. Its pod carried a culture, a store of biomass and a
few technicians, and it set down where the biters were already thickest. Soon the field's first spawner was no
longer wild. It went on eating pollution as before, but the biters it bred now were striped in green and yellow,
and they followed a plan.

The company's engineers farm the swarm. Smoke from your chimneys drifts over the creep and settles there, and the
creep turns it into the next wave. The more you build, the faster the culture breeds.

Those who held out against the early waves describe them in the same terms. A lone scout circles the wall at a
distance and leaves. Some time later the wave arrives at a gate other than the last one. It walks past the turrets
it does not need to fight and goes for the poles and inserters behind them.

::: {.pullquote cite="A survivor's log"}
The wall held, and the next wave came for the wall.
:::

When a wall holds, Synthexis remembers it. The next wave sent that way brings bursters bred for the purpose and
waits for them before it moves. Where mines lie on its way in, the culture breeds sweepers to clear them.

It keeps a truce with the wild biters and with Grubstake, whose drills feed it. A culture that loses its clinic stops
improving its breeds, and an incubator cut off from the creep goes back to the wild. Somewhere farther out, another
field of spawners waits for a carrier.
:::

# Kessler-Hayashi {faction="kessler-hayashi" kicker="The corporations"}

Kessler-Hayashi is a security contractor. It lands late and is at war with you from the day it arrives. Its
research happens in the world: a lab for each branch of its tree, each in a district of its own. A branch climbs,
and its units are fielded, only while its lab stands.

## Its units

::: {.unit unit="lp-tank"}
The backbone of every siege. Tanks come out in staggered ranks and stop just outside your guns' reach.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-railgunner"}
Its camps are clean of biters because of these. They are poor at anything else, and they are the ones carrying the
rail coils you want.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-lance"}
Fielded once your troopers have cost it enough. Its beam reaches past theirs, so a trooper line that won the last
fight loses the next one.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-laser-drone"}
Kessler-Hayashi's sky. They come with its second level, in small numbers, and they ignore walls.
:::

## How its army grows

::: {.tree tree="kh-units" kicker="Unit tree"}
Each research node is bought with parts once its trigger has fired: the units it answers have cost Kessler-Hayashi
enough. Dashed nodes are armor and siege abilities, not units. A node is bought, and its units fielded, only while
its lab stands.
:::

# Grubstake {faction="grubstake" kicker="The corporations"}

Grubstake is a mining concern that strips your ore and raids what your turrets do not cover. It usually lands
first, and it keeps coming.

::: {.unit unit="lp-grubstake-buggy"}
Fast, light and everywhere. Most of what Grubstake takes from you, it takes with buggies.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-grubstake-slug"}
Grubstake buys slugs after your vehicles have killed enough of its raiders.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-grubstake-dozer"}
A wall that has stopped Grubstake twice will meet a dozer the third time.
:::

::: {.fieldnote title="its claims"}
A claim marker makes Grubstake leave your buildings near it alone. Its pact with the wild biters is real: inside a
Grubstake claim, the biters do not attack Grubstake's machines.
:::

# Your army {faction="player"}

You can raise an army of your own. How many units you field is set by command bandwidth, which no amount of items
can buy.

::: {.unit unit="lp-trooper"}
Cheap, quick to train and quick to lose. Troopers win against raiders and lose against lasers.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-battle-tank"}
The answer to a walled camp. It takes the longest to train.
:::

::: {.tree tree="player-techs" kicker="Tech tree"}
What the wreckage teaches you. Each column is the company whose wreckage or field study a technology comes from; each
band is the base-game military technology it waits for. Arrows mark the faction technologies that need another.
:::
